fixes.explanation: Blood it is. The writer says the high priest never entered without it, and he offered it for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance (Hebrews 9:7). He didn't just show up and hope for the best. Only the high priest went into that second room, and only once a year.

True, and notice who's doing the showing: the Holy Spirit. The writer says that by this arrangement, the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing. So the tabernacle itself was showing something. I think that's worth a second look.

Yes, a greater and more perfect tabernacle, one that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation. The writer says Christ went through it as high priest of the good things that have come. That's the tabernacle in verse 11. Quite a contrast with the earthly sanctuary in verse 1.

Gold shows up in this passage, but it belongs to the earthly tabernacle, like the gold-covered ark and the gold jar of manna. The tabernacle Christ goes through is greater and more perfect. The writer says it is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation. Gold isn't part of how he describes it.

Zion isn't mentioned in this passage. The writer says Christ went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation. That's how the text describes it. A place on a map isn't part of that description.

By His own blood. The writer says Christ did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption. That's the big contrast with the high priest, who offered blood for himself and for the people (Hebrews 9:7). Christ entered by His own.

Eternal. The writer says Christ entered once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption. The high priest went in once a year, but Christ entered once for all. That's the redemption He secured.
Partial isn't the word the writer uses. Christ entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption. The word is eternal. That's what the text says He secured.

Christ Himself. The writer says that through the eternal Spirit, He offered Himself unblemished to God. He is the one who offered, and He offered Himself. That's why His blood can purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God.
